scope: Proposition 3.9 (Pattern comparison) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 26-27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix regular compact sets Qi and filled buffered neigh- borhoods Bi, 1 ≤ i ≤ m, with the Bi pairwise disjoint and a fixed positive separation between Qi and ∂Bi. Assume each Bi is contained in the domain, with no prescribed data there other than 26 the pattern being tested in Qi. Exterior data may be arbitrary admissible (s, W) data and their retained connections. There is a constant C such that, for complete patterns pi, C−m m Y i=1 πi(pi) ≤ µ[pi on every Qi] ≤ Cm m Y i=1 πi(pi). (3.20) Here µ is any such conditional flat law, and πi is the plane pattern law in Qi. The constant depends on the fixed buffer geometry and t, not on the patterns or on their number of microscopic prescriptions. Copies under parity-preserving lattice translations and reflections satisfy the same assertion. In particular, the single-box pattern laws have uniformly bounded Radon–Nikodym density ratios, and the same remains true locally after conditioning on any collection of separated patterns in the other boxes.
